stage_a.note: They are incredibly energetic, smiling broadly, shouting with excitement, and high-fiving each other during the pitch.
Both founders show intense, sustained excitement about their product, using expansive gestures and dynamic vocal delivery.
They are extremely friendly, laughing together, and directly engaging the panel with a highly approachable demeanor.

venture.description: A versatile, gourmet seafood breading mix that can be baked, air-fried, or deep-fried, sold directly to consumers and in retail stores.
venture.note: They sell directly at festivals and wholesale to major grocery chains.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and enthusiastically describe their versatile seafood breading mix.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin claps and laughs in response to their high-energy presentation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert remarks on how excited the founders are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe transitions the pitch to handing out the food samples.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda hands out the samples, explaining the different types of food that have been breaded and fried.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert praises the chicken, calling it fantastic.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin comments that the shrimp is very good.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond states that they complete him after tasting the food.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks to see the packaging.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they have applied the mix to vegetables.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if the product can be used to fry anything.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda confirms that it can be applied to vegetables and that the packaging shows different applications.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for their business numbers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda details the cost to make a bag, the direct-to-consumer price, the wholesale price, and the retail price.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their lifetime sales are to date.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda states they have sold four hundred and nine thousand dollars worth of product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks what they project to do in sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda projects finishing the year at two hundred and seventy thousand dollars, and next year at four hundred and fifty thousand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they have done any on-site or on-premise sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda confirms they do on-premise sales, explaining that every week they can be found selling somewhere.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks how Joe and Maranda came up with the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe explains his blue-collar background, his passion for the restaurant business, getting money from his dad, and opening a restaurant.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda shares the story of how they met when she went to sell him advertising, and he predicted they would marry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe recounts seeing her eight years later at a festival and asking if she was married yet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda says he predicted she would be married soon, and two weeks later she had a ring on her finger.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks how long Joe was in the restaurant business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe replies that the restaurants did very well and they ended up opening six locations.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks if the restaurants are still operating.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe confirms that the restaurants are absolutely not still going.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe explains that Hurricane Katrina hit and shut them down, but they saved two fryers and started selling at festivals.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks how long they have been doing that.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda answers that they have been doing it for about fifteen years.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe adds that he still has fryers in the car and is still frying fish.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if they were selling the product in grocery stores or just driving around to festivals.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda explains that at a festival people wanted to take the mix home, which sparked the idea to bag and sell it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how long ago they started bagging and selling it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda states this is their third year, and they have expanded from eight local stores to eight hundred stores nationwide.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori remarks that getting into that many stores is really hard to do.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks how much of their own money they have invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Maranda answers that they have invested a total of fifty thousand dollars from the family.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks about the ownership structure and the dad's stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe replies that his dad owns eighty-five percent and he owns fifteen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe explains that it's a tight-knit family business, his credit was zero, so his dad fronted the money.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the valuation, pointing out that asking for a million dollar valuation implies a twenty-five multiple, which is unheard of.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe argues that Kevin is missing the consumer aspect, asserting that they have an army of consumers driving the value.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin retorts that Joe Junior is not worth a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Daymond if he'd bet, hears Daymond wants fifty percent, and then declares he is out due to valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori praises the food and their hustle but says the business isn't right for her to invest in, so she's out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark explains that cooking isn't his thing, so the product doesn't fit him, and he exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert says he can't invest when the dad owns eighty-five percent and he won't make an offer they'd like, so he's out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond relates to their hustle of selling on corners, understands the customer, and offers the requested money for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe counters Daymond's offer, asking if he would do eighteen percent instead.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond immediately rejects the eighteen percent counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe asks if Daymond will stand firm at twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond confirms that he requires twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Joe excitedly accepts Daymond's offer of twenty-five percent.

decisions.note: Valuation is too high and he would need too much equity.
She likes them but feels it's not the right business for her to invest in.
He doesn't cook and the product doesn't fit his lifestyle.
He can't invest with the dad owning 85% and doesn't want to make an offensive offer.
He understands their hustle and the target consumer.
Tries to negotiate a lower equity stake.
Accepts Daymond's firm offer after the counter is rejected.

record.notes: The pitch features extremely high energy and a long backstory. The founders share presentation duties effectively.
